$comment: An interpolation is the language's, wherever it lands. Inside an embedded shell region the shell grammar's own rules start earlier on the line and swallow it -- a command statement covers its arguments, a quoted string covers its contents -- and a pattern listed beside them cannot win, because TextMate takes the earliest match and not the first-listed one. An injection is the mechanism for exactly this: `L:` puts it ahead of the host grammar's patterns at every position.
